title: AWS Cloud Support Internship: What I Actually Practiced

cover.alt: Conceptual training-lab illustration tracing an upload through processing and stored records.

figures.title: A repeatable cloud-lab troubleshooting loop
figures.summary: The internship’s practical method was to locate a failing boundary, test a fix, and record the result.

items.label: Reproduce
items.detail: Run the same trigger and confirm the failure.

items.label: Read logs
items.detail: Find the exact error and stack trace.

items.label: Check access
items.detail: Inspect roles, policies, and trust relationships.

items.label: Validate
items.detail: Rerun the trigger after the change.

items.label: Document
items.detail: Write down the cause and the fix.

figures.caption: This sequence describes guided training labs, not ownership of customer production incidents.

figures.title: What the capstone connected
figures.summary: A small event-driven chain made each connection visible and testable.

items.label: Upload
items.detail: A user supplies a sample file.

items.label: S3 event
items.detail: The bucket event starts the next step.

items.label: Lambda
items.detail: The function extracts metadata from the object.

items.label: DynamoDB
items.detail: A permitted write stores the metadata record.

items.label: Frontend
items.detail: The Amplify-hosted interface reads and displays the records through its configured data path.

figures.caption: A schematic of the capstone described in the article, not a screenshot of a production deployment.
